title: Bayern Munich 1-1 Koln: Kane and Olise injured in Bundesliga draw
subtitle: With Harry Kane and Michael Olise both going off with injuries, it was not the return Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany had hoped for.
paragraphs: Harry Kane and Michael Olise both suffered injuries as Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by Koln in the Bundesliga.

Nathaniel Brown cancelled out Mikey Moore opener at Allianz Arena, where Vincent Kompany made his return to the sidelines after his illness, but Bayern settled for a point, giving Borussia Dortmund the opportunity to go top on Saturday.

Koln took a shock lead after just 12 minutes. Linton Maina led the swift counter-attack down the left wing before playing in Said El Mala, whose backheel was taken in by Moore before the Tottenham loanee rounded Urbig and scored.
Kane was forced off with an injury in the 20th minute, but Bayern started to pile on the pressure as his replacement Tom Bischof, Brown and Joshua Kimmich all tried their luck from range.
And it was a shot from outside the box which eventually beat Marvin Schwabe in the 37th minute, as Brown worked room from 20 yards out and curled into the bottom-right corner to restore parity.

Bayern were dealt another blow when Olise was taken off at half-time, while a poor miss from makeshift striker Lennart Karl was followed up by a stunning double save at the other end from Urbig to deny El Mala and Maina.

Jamal Musiala came off the bench for his first appearance since September and almost scored in the 80th minute, but was kept out by a last-ditch block, though Bayern breathed a sigh of relief soon after as El Mala inexplicably missed the target from close range.

With Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari already sidelined through injury, in addition to Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer, the last thing Kompany needed was injuries to his two best attackers in Kane and Olise.

Bayern mustered just 0.94 expected goals (xG) from their 17 shots, with 11 of those attempts coming from outside the box as they struggled to break down Koln, while their only shot on target was Brown's first-half goal.
Brown's strike was, however, Bayern's eighth goal of this Bundesliga season from outside the penalty area - the most by any team in Europe's top-five leagues in 2026-27.

The hosts at one point featured an unfamiliar front four of Brown, Bischof, Tim Binder, who made his Bundesliga debut, and Karl, before Musiala made his long-awaited return off the bench, and their inexperience showed against a resolute Koln defence.

The visitors will perhaps feel they should have taken all three points with their counter-attacking display, accumulating 1.98 xG from their seven shots, four of which tested Urbig, and El Mala showed his frustration following his miss after being replaced late on.
Nevertheless, the point moves Koln three points clear of the relegation zone ahead of the weekend's action, and they can certainly take plenty of positives from this result.
